sections.h2: What is the address and schedule for the Saginaw County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
The office sits inside the Saginaw County Courthouse at 111 S. Michigan Avenue, Saginaw, MI 48602. The office page gives Monday to Friday service from 8:00 until a quarter to five, excluding holidays. The phone is (989) 790-5270 and the fax is (989) 790-5278. The page still carries an old note about a lunch closing that ended in November 2022, so confirm the counter schedule by phone before a trip downtown.

The county's description of the job is short: the register is the official keeper of every real property record in the county, indexes what is recorded, holds the original plats of subdivisions, and helps cities and townships with liber and page numbers and property descriptions. Staff cannot draft a document or answer legal questions, a point the office repeats on its quitclaim deed form page.

Saginaw County covers 816 square miles, 800 of them land, and its seat is the city of Saginaw. The 2020 census counted 190,124 residents and 85,953 housing units, with 8.7% of the units vacant and 70.5% of occupied homes owned by the people living in them.

sections.h2: How much does recording cost in Saginaw County?
sections.html:
Each document costs $30 to record, regardless of page count, under MCL 600.2567. A document that assigns or discharges more than one instrument adds $3 for each extra instrument. Other charges on the county fee page:

  • Copies at $1 a page, and $5 a document for certification.
  • Searches at the counter at $5 each.
  • A public workstation in the office at no charge.
  • Tax certification, which comes from the County Treasurer and not from the register.

The office takes cash, check, money order and the four major credit cards, and card payments carry a fee. The Treasurer's certification fee, listed on the same county checklist, is $5 for up to five descriptions and $1 for each description after that. Ask the Treasurer's office, at 111 S. Michigan, Room 107, whether a certificate is needed for your instrument before you stand in line at the register.

sections.h2: What format rules can get a Saginaw County deed rejected?
sections.html:
The county publishes a long checklist drawn from Michigan's recording statutes, and a document that misses any item can be turned away. The items below are the ones that most often decide whether a deed signed after 1997 is accepted.

Saginaw County recording checklist, summarized from the register's quitclaim deed page
ItemWhat the checklist requires
Paper and typeWhite paper of at least 20 pounds, legible, in 10-point type or larger
Page sizeAt least 8.5 by 11 inches and no larger than 8.5 by 14
Margins2.5 inches clear at the top of page one and half an inch on every other side
Title lineFirst line names the single recordable event the paper evidences
SignaturesOriginal, in black or dark blue ink, with the name printed beneath
Notary blockDated acknowledgment, printed notary name and commission expiration
Legal descriptionPlat caption and lot number, or quarter section, section, town and range if unplatted

The checklist adds a few more items. The grantee's street or post office address must appear, the drafter's name and address must appear, and the first five digits of any Social Security number must be obscured on instruments signed after September 12, 2017. A document partly in another language needs an English translation attached.

sections.h2: How is transfer tax handled on a Saginaw County deed?
sections.html:
The county's checklist says the tax is collected at $8.60 for every $1,000 of consideration. A taxable deed must show the total consideration on its face, or the parties file a Real Estate Transfer Valuation Affidavit with it. A deed that owes nothing must name the exemption it relies on.

Under the state act, the seller is the liable party, and the county treasurer receives payment inside 15 days after the instrument is delivered (MCL 207.523). The exemption list in MCL 207.526 covers, among others, a land contract under which title has not yet passed, a deed that straightens a boundary with no money changing hands, a conveyance of mineral rights, and any transfer between spouses that creates or ends a tenancy by the entirety.

Some papers carry their own proof requirements. A deed that mentions a survivor needs a certified death certificate recorded as its own document or already recorded and referenced by liber and page. Court orders must be certified and sealed by the clerk of court. A release or assignment must cite the original liber and page or document number.

sections.h2: Which Saginaw County places and roads shape local sales?
sections.html:
Saginaw County grew along the Saginaw River. A footpath that became the Saginaw Trail was authorized in 1819 and reached the city of Saginaw in 1841, one of Michigan's earliest roads. Today I-75 and I-675 pass through the area, with US 23, M-13, M-46 and M-47 linking the western suburbs to the airport at Freeland. The county was organized in 1835, and its communities include the cities of Saginaw, Frankenmuth and Zilwaukee plus dozens of townships.

Saginaw Valley State University is in Kochville Township, and Delta College serves the county from nearby Bay County. Parcels can sit in one of about twenty school districts, from Saginaw Public Schools and Saginaw Township Community Schools to Frankenmuth, Chesaning Union and Birch Run Area Schools.

Saginaw County is part of a three-county metro area with Midland and Bay City. The 2020 median age was 41.3, and one in five residents had reached 65.

sections.h2: What does the Saginaw County Treasurer add to a deed transfer?
sections.html:
The Treasurer's office is in Room 107 of the courthouse at 111 S. Michigan, with weekday hours of 8:00 am to 5:00 pm. It collects the county's delinquent real property taxes, runs the Delinquent Tax Revolving Fund, and chairs the Land Bank Authority that manages tax foreclosed property. State law bars the register from recording most warranty deeds without a treasurer's certificate (MCL 211.135).

For back taxes the Treasurer takes payment in person, by mail or online. Online payments run through a third-party processor and carry an access fee on the total. A card payment that is later reversed voids the payment, and the fees and interest reapply back to the original date.

sections.h2: What should a seller do before the Saginaw County recording step?
sections.html:
Gather the paperwork in an order that matches how the county handles it:

  • Read the parcel's current deed and legal description at the register's public workstation, free of charge.
  • Ask the County Treasurer whether a certificate is needed and pay its fee separately.
  • Put the full consideration on the deed or prepare the valuation affidavit, and bring the transfer tax payment.
  • Check margins, ink color, notary block and the grantee's address against the county checklist.
  • Bring $30 for each document and phone the office to confirm the card fee and counter hours.

The register also notifies local assessors of transfers, and the buyer files its own transfer form with the assessor within 45 days. On transfer, the parcel's taxable value resets to state equalized value for the following year (MCL 211.27a).

faqs.q: How much is a recording fee at the Saginaw County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: It is $30 per document, with $3 added for each extra instrument a single document assigns or discharges. Copies are $1 a page and certification is $5 a document.

faqs.q: Can the Register of Deeds help me write a deed?
faqs.a: No. The office says it cannot prepare documents or give legal advice. Its quitclaim deed page sells a blank form for $5 plus an access fee and points owners to an attorney for legal help.

faqs.q: What does the county checklist say about transfer tax?
faqs.a: It lists $8.60 for each $1,000 of consideration. The seller owes the tax, and an exempt transfer has to name its exemption on the instrument itself.

faqs.q: Where do I get a tax certificate for a Saginaw County deed?
faqs.a: From the Saginaw County Treasurer, not the register. The treasurer's fee on the county checklist is $5 for up to five descriptions and $1 for each one beyond that.

faqs.q: What phone number reaches the Saginaw County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: Call (989) 790-5270. The office is at 111 S. Michigan Avenue in Saginaw, and the fax line is (989) 790-5278.
